claim_formal: ∀ q≥1, ∀ Dirichlet character χ mod q, ∀ s∈ℂ: Re s > 7/8 ∧ ¬(χ principal ∧ s=1) → L(s,χ) ≠ 0 (same for every finite-order Hecke L-function over ℚ(√-3))

quote_A.text: Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ has no zero in $\Re s>7/8$. The same holds for every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$.

quote_B.text: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} resolves the quasi-Riemann hypothesis affirmatively

notes: Matrix is borderline M4 (no zeros) vs M8 (explicit bound sup Re ρ ≤ 7/8); chose M4 since the statement is non-vanishing. Lean comparators match (zeta and Dirichlet versions). Companion results: alternate 11/12 proof (O9-like), uniform Landau–Siegel zero exclusion (Lean SiegelZeros); corollaries: Vinogradov least-nonresidue conjecture, deterministic square roots, effective class-number bounds.

claim_formal: ∀ compact Fujiki-class-C manifold X, ∀ rational SNC boundary Δ, ∀ connected-fiber surjection f:X→Y onto a normal compact complex space: κ(X,K_X+Δ) ≥ κ(F,K_F+Δ_F) + κ(f|Δ) (F very general fiber)

quote_A.text: \kappa(X,K_X+\Delta) \geq\kappa(F,K_F+\Delta_F)+\kappa(f\mid\Delta).

quote_B.text: We prove Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for rational simple normal crossing boundaries on compact manifolds in Fujiki class $`\mathcal C`$

notes: Family bundles: orbifold subadditivity (headline), Popa's logarithmic variation conjecture (Iitaka–Viehweg), reverse log Kodaira inequality and log additivity (Popa conj 3.9, restricted setting), ordinary Iitaka C_{n,m} over char-0 fields, b-semiampleness for Kähler fibrations. Lean comparator (LogKodairaFiberNegative) appears to formalize a piece of the reverse-log-Kodaira paper, not the headline; truncated in input.

claim_formal: For the explicit A = ℂ[p,s,u,F,J]/(H): A is a 4-dim domain, A[w] ≅ ℂ^[5] and A ≇ ℂ^[4]

quote_A.text: \[ A[w]\simeq\kk\poly5, \qquad A\not\simeq\kk\poly4. \] Consequently the Zariski cancellation problem over the complex numbers has a negative answer in dimension four.

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to Zariski's affine-space cancellation problem over ℂ in dimension four.

notes: Prefix: Lean statement is closed about the explicit A (none); read as 'there is a fourfold X' it would be ∃. Also disproves Stable Coordinate Conjecture (dim 5) and Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture over A^1, A^2. Only dimension four over ℂ, but the problem (does cancellation hold?) is answered no.

claim_formal: ∀ f ∈ L log L(𝕋): for a.e. x ∈ 𝕋, S_N f(x) → f(x) as N→∞

quote_A.text: For every complex-valued $f\in L\log L(\mathbb T)$, there is a measurable set $N_f$ of measure zero such that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}S_Nf(x)=f(x)

quote_B.text: This establishes the classical $`L\log L`$ sufficiency conjecture.

notes: Lean: ∀ f, ∃ null set E, ∀ x∉E — encodes 'almost every x' (∀ᵍ). Corollary: weak-L^1 maximal bound in Luxemburg norm.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth nonnegative completely monotone g, ∀ locally finite C ⊂ ℝ² of centered disk density 1: E_g(C) ≥ E_g(A₂) (triangular lattice), i.e. min energy = E_g(A₂)

quote_A.text: latticeEnergy g ≤ energy g C ∧ latticeEnergy g = energy g A

quote_B.text: Their Euclidean conjecture singled out the triangular, $E_8$, and Leech lattices \citep[Conjecture~9.4]{CohnKumar2007}.

notes: Matrix M9 (lattice attains the minimum value) vs M1 (inequality between given objects). Problem taken as the planar case of Cohn–Kumar universal optimality; the paper does not literally say 'resolves conjecture' for the headline. Bundled: Cohn–Elkies planar sharpness (sharp Fourier certificate, M2), Sandier–Serfaty conjecture (Coulomb renormalized energy), Brauchart–Hardin–Saff linear term on S² (M9 asymptotic formula), Riesz 0<s<2.

claim_formal: L = RL = BPL

quote_A.text: \[ \Lclass=\RL=\BPL. \]

quote_B.text: We prove $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$, resolving the derandomization problem for polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space.

notes: B.problem: the 'derandomization problem' L=BPL is a widely held conjecture (P1); could be read as P2. Also acceptance-probability approximation in deterministic O(log n + q) space.

claim_formal: ω_ℂ ≤ 9/4 (∀ε>0: n×n complex matrices multiplied in O_ε(n^{9/4+ε}) operations)

quote_A.text: Arithmetic.omega ℂ ≤ (9 : ℝ) / 4

quote_B.text: Dupont et al. report $\omega<2.371177$ by optimizing this combination-loss framework~\cite{Dup26}.

notes: Companions: ω<2.258, α>0.465, ω(1,0.709,1)<2.092 in char 0; ω_F<2.371054886006746 over every field. Record improvement, not settling ω=2.

claim_formal: ∃ L ∈ P (polytime TM decides L) such that ∀ A>0, ∀^∞ n: S₃(f_n) > 2^{A√n} (OR–AND–OR total gate count)

quote_A.text: \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 S_3(f_n)}{\sqrt n}=\infty.

quote_B.text: This is the depth-three lower-bound problem discussed by Gurumukhani, Paturi, Pudl\'ak, Saks, and Talebanfard~\cite[Section~1.1]{GPPST24} and still identified as open

notes: A.matrix: superpolynomial-in-√n circuit lower bound; M8 (one-sided rate) vs M10 (hardness/computational status). B: could also be P4/O7 (crossing the 2^{Θ(√n)} record); paper says it is weaker than the HJP95 2^{n^{1/2+ε}} question, which stays open. I read the posed question 'can one P language beat 2^{A√n} for every A?' as P2 answered yes.

claim_formal: ∀ finite family φ_i(x)=r_i x+t_i on ℝ with 0<|r_i|<1, ∀ positive probability vector p: dim_H μ_{Φ,p} = min{1, h_RW/χ}

quote_A.text: \dim_H\mu_{\Phi,p} =\min\left\{1,\frac{h_{\mathrm{RW}}(\Phi,p)}{\chi(\Phi,p)}\right\}.

quote_B.text: This resolves the entropy-rate dimension conjecture.

notes: Exact formula (M9). Corollaries: no-overlap entropy/Lyapunov formula, attractor dimension, homogeneous systems (Lean SelfSimilarCorollaries).

claim_formal: For the explicit 35-vertex, 66-edge bipartite incidence graph H: ∃ finite simple graph G with ≥1 edge such that t(H,G) < p(G)^66

quote_A.text: ∃ size : ℕ, 0 < size ∧ ∃ host : SimpleGraph (Fin size), (∃ left right, host.Adj left right) ∧ homDensity H host < (edgeDensity host) ^ 66

quote_B.text: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges

notes: H explicit, G existential. finite_checkable: a witness G is verifiable by finite computation. Corollaries: amplification (ratio arbitrarily small), failure of the Skokan–Thoma forcing conjecture.

claim_formal: For the explicit 66×66 binary H: ∀ c,C>0 ∃ n, ε∈(0,1), A∈{0,1}^{n×n}: dist_H(A) ≥ ε ∧ N_H(A) < c ε^C n^132

quote_A.text: ∀ c C : ℝ, 0 < c → 0 < C → ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 ∧ ∃ A : BinaryMatrix n, fixedDistance A ≥ ε ∧ (copyCount fixedH A : ℝ) < c * Real.rpow ε C * ((n : ℝ) ^ 132)

quote_B.text: This disproves the polynomial ordered binary matrix-removal conjecture.

notes: Prefix follows Lean (H fixed explicitly); if the pattern H is counted as a witness the prefix is ∃∀∃. Paper also gives explicit sequence n_h, ε_h. Corollary: canonical-tester lower bound q ≥ exp(Ω(ε^{-1/2})); answers Alon–Ben-Eliezer finite-family question negatively.

claim_formal: ∃ finite-dimensional unital ℂ-algebra A such that ∀ m≥1 ∃ f.d. left A-module N_m: 2m−2 ≤ pd_A N_m < ∞ (so findim A = ∞)

quote_A.text: There is a finite-dimensional unital complex algebra \(A\) such that, for every integer \(m\ge1\), there is a finite-dimensional left \(A\)-module \(N_m\) with \[ 2m-2\le\pd_A N_m<\infty. \]

quote_B.text: This disproves the little finitistic-dimension conjecture.

notes: Prefix ∃∀∃ from Lean (A, m, N); the bare headline 'findim A = ∞' would be ∃. Corollary: extreme left–right asymmetry (findim Λ = ∞, findim Λ^op = 0), injectives do not generate D(Mod Λ). Companion characteristic-2 example cited (OpenAITachikawa2026) but not used.

claim_formal: ∀ α>0, ∀ bounded Borel f: lim_{N→∞} E p_N(f) = inf_{q∈Q}{α V_f(q) + S_I(q)}, and p_N(f) → that value in probability (Gaussian Ising perceptron)

quote_A.text: \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb E p_N(f) =\mathcal P_f(\alpha) :=\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q}\{\alpha V_f(q)+S_{\mathrm I}(q)\}.

quote_B.text: The density restrictions in these predecessors are substantive and are absent from Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

notes: B is uncertain: the free energy at all densities is a long-standing open problem with physics (replica/Gardner) predictions; no named conjecture is cited in the input, so P2/O1, but O8 (extends Talagrand/Bolthausen et al. small-density results) is defensible. Bundled: spherical perceptron free energy (Lean PerceptronFreeEnergy), bi-orthogonally invariant disorder, microscopic jamming at margin −1 (threshold α_c, exponents γ, θ).

quote_A.text: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (S : Set (Fin n → ℕ)), REPred (fun a => a ∈ S) → ∃ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m ∧ ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin n ⊕ Fin m) ℤ, Represents P S

quote_B.text: This proves the single-fold conjecture and, consequently, the finite-fold conjecture.

notes: Corollary: Hilbert's 10th problem stays undecidable under an at-most-one-solution promise (M10).

claim_formal: ∀ f.g. virtually polycyclic P, ∀ f.g. group H: H ~_QI P → H virtually polycyclic

quote_A.text: Let $P$ be a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group, and let $H$ be any finitely generated group. If $H$ and $P$ are quasi-isometric, then $H$ is virtually polycyclic.

quote_B.text: This resolves the lattice-recognition conjecture of Eskin, Fisher and Whyte

notes: Corollary: lattice-recognition formulation (virtually a uniform lattice in some simply connected solvable Lie group). Uniform bounded-height theorem for self-QIs of triangulable unimodular Lie groups.

claim_formal: ∀ γ∈(1/2,3/2), ∀ m≥1, ∀ measurable Hermitian W≥0 (m×m) with ∫tr W^{γ+1/2}<∞: Tr(H_W)_-^γ ≤ C_γ ∫ tr W^{γ+1/2}, with C_γ the scalar one-bound-state constant, optimal and attained

quote_A.text: The constant is optimal in every matrix dimension. With $r=(\gamma-1/2)^{-1}$, it is attained by

quote_B.text: We resolve affirmatively the remaining cases of the scalar one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring conjecture: for every $`\frac12\lt \gamma\lt \frac32`$, the optimal constant is the one-bound-state constant.

notes: Headline per summary is the matrix version (stronger than the scalar conjecture); Lean comparator (MainClaim) is the scalar sharp inequality plus attainment. Scalar paper resolves remaining cases of the 1D Lieb–Thirring conjecture (O1); matrix version could also be coded O8. restricted_range: γ∈(1/2,3/2), 1D. Bundled: classification of all equality cases (M6).

claim_formal: L(F_2) ≅ L(F_3) as tracial von Neumann algebras

quote_A.text: There exists a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism \[ \Phi:L(\F_2)\longrightarrow L(\F_3). \]

quote_B.text: We solve the free group factor isomorphism problem affirmatively by proving that $`L(\mathbb F_2)`$ and $`L(\mathbb F_3)`$ are isomorphic

notes: Corollaries: all interpolated free group factors incl. L(F_∞) isomorphic, fundamental group ℝ_{>0}, free entropy dimension not an invariant (negative answer to Voiculescu). Rank-step theorem L(F_n)≅L(F_{n+1}) for n≥3. Lean comparator (InterpolatedFactors) truncated in input.

claim_formal: ∃ unital infinite-dimensional simple C*-algebra A with a faithful tracial state such that all nonzero irreducible representations of A are unitarily equivalent (hence A ≇ K(H))

quote_A.text: There exists a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra $A$ with a faithful tracial state such that all its nonzero irreducible representations are unitarily equivalent.

quote_B.text: Tanaka gives another ZFC construction with a faithful tracial state \cite[Theorems~1.1, 4.1 and~5.3]{Tanaka2026}, so the existence conclusion of Theorem~\ref{na:main} is already present there.

notes: Answers Naimark's problem negatively in ZFC, but the summary and intro say this is an alternative to Tanaka's prior ZFC construction, so O9 (new proof). If Tanaka's result is not counted as prior, O2.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥1, ∀ connected Hausdorff second-countable topological n-manifold M (no boundary), ∀ locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group G acting faithfully and jointly continuously on M: G is a Lie group

quote_A.text: A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological \(n\)-manifold without boundary is a Lie group.

quote_B.text: We prove the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension

notes: Key theorem: every action of ℤ_p on such a manifold has nonzero kernel (M4); the Lie conclusion uses the classical reduction. Corollary: almost periodic homeomorphisms embed in flows (Pardon Conj. 1.4).

claim_formal: ∀ Grothendieck coherator C (Ara–Henry convention): the homotopy theory of weak globular C-∞-groupoids is equivalent to the homotopy theory of spaces

quote_A.text: its weak globular infinity-groupoids recover the homotopy theory of spaces

quote_B.text: We prove the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention

notes: The paper's main theorem (and the Lean comparator GrothendieckElementaryExpansion) is Henry's pushout conjecture: elementary expansions of cellular C-∞-groupoids are weak equivalences; the homotopy hypothesis follows via Henry's semi-model-structure framework (hence full_only_with_prior_results). Scope: the Ara–Henry coherator convention, not every possible formulation.

claim_formal: Con(ZFC + measurable cardinal) → SQ_𝔽 is independent of ZFC, for 𝔽 ∈ {ℝ, ℂ} (ZFC ⊢ (𝔠 real-valued measurable → SQ_𝔽) and ZFC ⊢ (CH → ¬SQ_𝔽))

quote_A.text: We prove that this statement is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal.

quote_B.text: The separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient.

notes: conditional_on: ["Con(ZFC + measurable cardinal)"] (standard large-cardinal hypothesis for relative consistency). Lean comparator covers only the CH ⇒ ¬SQ half. Corollary: density-ℵ1 version independent relative to Con(ZFC) alone.

claim_formal: ∀ closed connected smooth 4-manifold X, ∀ smooth almost complex J on X: (∃ symplectic ω taming J) → (∃ symplectic ω' compatible with J)

quote_A.text: Suppose that a smooth almost complex structure \(J\) on a closed connected smooth real four-manifold \(X\) is tamed by a symplectic form. Then there is a smooth symplectic form compatible with \(J\).

quote_B.text: This gives a positive solution to Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture.

notes: Corollary: description of the compatible cone via the taming cone; b_2^+=1 gives K^t_J = K^c_J.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2, ∀ K∈ℝ, ∀ noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space (X,d,H^n), ∀ p∈X with all tangents ≅ ℝ^n: ∃ open U∋p, open V⊆ℝ^n, homeomorphism F:U→V that is bi-Lipschitz (constant L_n depending only on n)

quote_A.text: then there exist an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(p\), an open set \(V\subset\R^n\), and a homeomorphism \(F:U\to V\) such that \[ L_n^{-1}d(x,z)\le |F(x)-F(z)|\le L_nd(x,z)

quote_B.text: We resolve the regular-point bi-Lipschitz conjecture in the noncollapsed setting.

notes: The theorem has a uniform constant: ∀n ∃L_n ∀(K,X,p) ∃(U,V,F), i.e. prefix ∀∃∀∃ if L_n counts. The OpenAI summary speaks of a 'point-dependent finite constant', which is weaker than the paper's L_n. Corollary: full-measure open manifold region with a countable bi-Lipschitz atlas.

claim_formal: d_* = 7, i.e. (∀ d≤6, ∀ nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer u of the one-phase Bernoulli energy on ℝ^d: u flat) ∧ (∃ nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer on ℝ^7)

quote_A.text: Consequently, \[ d_*=7. \]

quote_B.text: Our main result answers positively the critical-dimension question whether $d_*=7$.

notes: Threshold (M9). Prefix: closed statement d_*=7; its components are ∀ (flatness for d≤6) and ∃ (dim 7). The dim-7 existence was already known (De Silva–Jerison 2009); the Lean comparator (nonflat_in_seven) formalizes that known half. New content is flatness in d=5,6 (prior d_*≥5 from Jerison–Savin). Could also be read as P4/O1 (closing the gap 5 ≤ d_* ≤ 7). Corollary: sharp singular-set bound dim Sing ≤ n−7.

claim_formal: ∀ u ∈ C²(ℝ⁸,(−1,1)) with Δu = u³−u and ∂₈u > 0: ∃ e∈S⁷ (e₈>0), c∈ℝ: u(x) = tanh((e·x−c)/√2)

quote_A.text: Then there are $e\in\mathbb S^7$ with $e_8>0$ and $c\in\R$ such that \[ u(x)=\tanh\!\left(\frac{e\cdot x-c}{\sqrt2}\right)

quote_B.text: We resolve De Giorgi's conjecture positively in dimension eight

notes: Matrix: rigidity / classification of all monotone solutions as planar (M6), alternatively M1 (property 'u is 1-D'). Dimension 8 is the sharp endpoint and implies the lower dimensions, so O1 for the whole conjecture (n ≤ 8) rather than O5. Stronger bundled result: classification of stable solutions on ℝ⁷ with no energy-growth assumption.
